items.title: iRobot taglia i prezzi dei Roomba: con il Black Friday si risparmiano fino a 200 euro
items.summary: Dal 16 al 30 novembre su irobot.it nove Roomba costano meno, dai compatti che lavano i pavimenti ai Max con la base che fa quasi tutto da sola ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Oggi parte il Black Friday di iRobot, che fino al 30 novembre mette in offerta nove Roomba sul negozio online irobot.it. Il pezzo più atteso è il top di gamma: il Roomba Max 875 Combo con base AutoWash che ottiene uno sconto di ben 200 euro rispetto al prezzo degli ultimi 30 giorni. All'altro capo del listino il Roomba 115 Combo scende a soli 149 euro, e in mezzo c'è un robot per ogni casa e per ogni budget. La spedizione è gratuita e c'è sempre il reso entro 30 giorni.

I modelli sono tanti, ma si "leggono" bene se li si guarda per serie. Inoltre, salendo di prezzo e di caratteristiche il robot si prende in carico sempre più lavoro, fino a lasciarci soltanto il compito di cambiare un sacchetto una volta ogni pochi mesi.

Quasi tutti i Roomba in offerta sono Combo , cioè aspirano e lavano il pavimento nella stessa passata . Si orientano con un sensore laser LiDAR che disegna la mappa della casa, così il robot pulisce per file ordinate, sa dove è già passato e dall'app Roomba Home si scelgono le stanze da pulire.

A fare la differenza, salendo di prezzo, è soprattutto la base di ricarica. La AutoEmpty aspira lo sporco raccolto dal robot e lo chiude in un sacchetto che si cambia ogni tre mesi circa. La AutoWash fa lo stesso lavoro e in più lava e asciuga i panni o il rullo lavapavimenti , così il robot riparte ogni volta pulito.

L'ultimo numero da tenere d'occhio è la potenza di aspirazione, misurata in pascal (Pa): indica la depressione creata dal motore, e più è alta più sporco il robot tira su da tappeti e fughe.

Nel Roomba Max 875 Combo + AutoWash iRobot ha messo il massimo della tecnologia . Per il Black Friday costa 799 euro, contro un listino di 1.199 euro. È disponibile nero o bianco.

Aspira con 35.000 Pa, il valore più alto di tutta l'offerta. Quando sale su un tappeto, la tecnologia SealForce abbassa da sola il modulo di aspirazione e rende la pulizia del tappeto fino a tre volte più efficace. Il rullo e la spazzola laterale sono anti-groviglio, pensati per chi convive con capelli lunghi e peli di cani e gatti.

Per lavare usa il rullo PowerSpin Max , che gira a 300 giri al minuto e preme sul pavimento con 18 newton.

Sulle macchie più ostinate il robot passa prima con ThermaMist , una nebbia a ultrasuoni di acqua scaldata a 60 °C che pretratta lo sporco secco.

Con PerfectEdge il rullo si allunga lateralmente di 45 mm per arrivare fino al battiscopa, mentre DriLift lo solleva quando il robot riconosce un tappeto, che così resta asciutto.

La navigazione unisce il LiDAR ClearView Pro a PrecisionVision AI , una telecamera che riconosce gli oggetti sul pavimento, come cavi e scarpe, e li aggira invece di trascinarli . Il robot è alto 9,98 cm, quindi passa sotto molti divani, e supera soglie fino a 3,5 cm .

La base AutoWash chiude il cerchio. Lava il rullo con acqua a 80 °C, lo asciuga con aria a 55 °C perché non resti umido, dosa da sola il detergente e svuota la polvere dal robot . Prima di doverla toccare passano fino a 90 giorni.

Chi vuole un Max spendendo 200 euro in meno trova il Roomba Max 775 Combo + AutoWash a 599 euro, 100 in meno degli ultimi 30 giorni, nei colori nero o bianco.

Rispetto all'875 rinuncia a poco , e conserva tutte le carte della serie Max: 30.000 Pa, due spazzole in gomma anti-groviglio, Dirt Detect per riconoscere le zone più sporche e Carpet Boost, che alza la potenza sui tappeti.

Lava con il rullo PowerSpin , protetto da una copertura che tiene asciutti i tappeti quando il robot li attraversa, e vede gli ostacoli con la stessa PrecisionVision AI dell'875. La sua base lava il rullo a 75 °C, lo asciuga a 50 °C e svuota la polvere fino a tre mesi .

Per le case con molti tappeti, dove il lavaggio non serve, c'è il Roomba Max 715 Vac + AutoEmpty , un aspirapolvere puro con gli stessi 30.000 Pa , le due spazzole in gomma, Dirt Detect e Carpet Boost del 775. La base AutoEmpty lo svuota per un massimo di 90 giorni . Durante il Black Friday costa 379 euro.

Il rullo PowerSpin scende di prezzo con la serie Plus 600, che lo usa con acqua a 60 °C e 15 newton di pressione. Entrambi i modelli aspirano con 30.000 Pa, riconoscono gli ostacoli con PrecisionVision AI e sono alti 9,95 cm.

Il Roomba Plus 615 Combo con base Wash Only ha lo sconto più forte di tutta la campagna in percentuale, circa il 27%: costa 399 euro, 150 in meno degli ultimi 30 giorni. È la strada più economica per avere il rullo lavapavimenti. La base lava il rullo a 80 °C e lo asciuga , ma non svuota la polvere , che comunque finisce in un sacchetto da un litro dentro il robot e basta per circa un mese .

Il Roomba Plus 675 Combo + AutoWash costa 549 euro, nero o bianco, e la differenza con il 615 sta tutta nella base. Questa svuota anche la polvere, lava il rullo a 80 °C, lo asciuga con aria a 55 °C e dosa il detergente, per arrivare fino a 90 giorni senza interventi . Sul robot c'è PerfectEdge, già visto sull'875, e una spazzola con un meccanismo taglia-peli che li accorcia mentre gira; in questo non resta avvolta e non c'è da liberarla con le forbici.

La serie Plus 400 e 500 è quella che entra dove gli altri restano fuori. Il 415 e il 575 sono alti appena 8,35 cm (il 21% in meno del Roomba Plus 505 della generazione precedente), e passano sotto letti, divani e mobili bassi dove la polvere si accumula indisturbata. Lavano con due panni rotanti DualClean da 200 giri al minuto, che si sollevano di 10 mm quando il robot riconosce un tappeto . Entrambi hanno la base AutoWash e sono disponibili in nero o bianco.

Il Roomba Plus 415 Combo + AutoWash scende a 299 euro. Aspira con 20.000 Pa e con SmartScrub preme di più sul pavimento per staccare le macchie secche. La base lava e asciuga i panni con aria calda, così non restano umidi fino al giro successivo .

Il Roomba Plus 575 Combo + AutoWash è l'occasione della fascia media: per il periodo promo costa 379 euro. Aspira con 25.000 Pa e porta su un robot così sottile la navigazione ClearView Pro con PrecisionVision AI, la stessa dei Max. La base lava i panni con acqua fino a 75 °C e poi li asciuga con aria calda.

Per cominciare a delegare la pulizia di casa basta il Roomba 115 Combo , che durante il Black Friday costa solo 149 euro, nero o bianco.

Ha la stessa navigazione laser dei modelli superiori , aspira con 15.000 Pa e lava con un panno in microfibra che si stacca e si lava.

È alto 9,2 cm e con una carica copre fino a 84 metri quadrati, cioè un appartamento di medie dimensioni.

Con 30 euro in più si smette anche di svuotarlo. Infatti, il Roomba 115 Combo + AutoEmpty costa 179 euro, ed è il modo più economico per avere un robot che si svuota da solo. La base raccoglie lo sporco in un sacchetto AllergenLock da 2,5 litri, che trattiene il 99% di pollini e muffe e dura circa tre mesi .

items.title: Colpito nella notte il ponte di Crimea, 'traffico bloccato'
items.summary: Mosca: 'Abbattuti 1.336 droni sulle regioni russe'
items.content:
Le forze armate ucraine hanno attaccato il ponte di Crimea e il traffico è bloccato fino a mezzogiorno, ha riferito il governatore della regione annessa dalla Federazione Russa nel 2014, Serghei Aksyonov. "Il nemico ha colpito il ponte di Crimea. Per questo motivo, il traffico sarà limitato fino a mezzogiorno circa. Sono stati dispiegati tutti i servizi necessari per far fronte all'emergenza ed è stato istituito un centro di risposta alle emergenze a Kerch", ha scritto Aksyonov su Telegram.

Il ministero della difesa russo ha riferito che "la scorsa notte scorsa, le forze di difesa aerea hanno intercettato e abbattuto 1.336 droni ucraini ad ala fissa sui territori delle regioni di Tver, Belgorod, Bryansk, Kursk, Kaluga, Tula, Ryazan, Oryol, Voronezh, Vladimir, Smolensk, Nizhny Novgorod, Rostov, Krasnodar, sulla Repubblica di Crimea (annessa nel 2014) su Mosca e sulle acque del Mar d'Azov e del Mar Nero".

items.title: Linux 7.4-rc3: correttivi per Zen 5, GPU e sensori
items.summary: Linux 7.4-rc3 introduce correttivi per AMD Zen 5, GPU Radeon, USB-C e sensori.
items.content:
Linux 7.4-rc3 è finalmente disponibile e vi diciamo subito che porta con sé alcuni aggiornamenti minori, ma importanti per chi utilizza processori AMD Zen 5 e schede grafiche Radeon.

Stando al changelog ufficiale, la terza versione di prova del nuovo kernel introduce una mitigazione di sicurezza per le CPU AMD più recenti, assieme a modifiche che potrebbero contribuire a ridurre i consumi energetici di alcune GPU compatibili. L'intervento sui processori Zen 5 riguarda TSA, ossia una vulnerabilità legata al comportamento interno della CPU che, in determinate condizioni, potrebbe consentire l'esposizione di informazioni sensibili.

Per quanto riguarda le schede grafiche Radeon, troviamo una serie di miglioramenti nella gestione delle frequenze e dell'alimentazione, ad esempio sono stati abilitati meccanismi come Multi-Coarse Gate Clock e Fine-Grain Clock Gating, che permettono di disattivare temporaneamente alcune sezioni del chip quando non vengono utilizzate.

items.title: Windows 11: una modifica nascosta rischia di rallentare il PC
items.summary: Una modifica nascosta promette di accelerare Windows 11, ma può rendere il PC più lento.
items.content:
Chi si ricorda i tempi in cui l'avvio di un PC era molto più lento di come avviene oggi? Le cose sono cambiate, e al di là della maggior velocità degli SSD e delle altre migliorie introdotte, da tempo circolano da tempo modifiche al registro di sistema che promettono di accelerare l'avvio delle applicazioni, ma a quanto pare una di queste, può produrre l'effetto opposto.

Dovete sapere che Windows 11 utilizza un meccanismo che distribuisce nel tempo l'esecuzione di alcuni programmi configurati per aprirsi automaticamente, ma invece di avviarli tutti nello stesso istante, il sistema può introdurre piccoli ritardi per evitare che processore, memoria e unità di archiviazione vengano sovraccaricati subito dopo l'accesso.

Alcuni utenti hanno individuato una modifica che permette di intervenire su questo comportamento. Il percorso interessato è HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer, all'interno del quale si può creare una chiave chiamata Serialize.

items.title: Disastro per Amazon Leo: Vulcan perde 40 satelliti in volo
items.summary: Vulcan fallisce dopo dieci minuti di volo: perduti tutti i 40 satelliti Amazon Leo.
items.content:
Mentre SpaceX registrava il più grande successo della sua storia aerospaziale, a distanza di poche ore un lancio che riguarda tecnologie Amazon non aveva la stessa sorte. Parliamo di quanto accaduto con il razzo Vulcan di United Launch Alliance, che ha fallito la sua missione domenica 15 novembre, causando la perdita di tutti e 40 i satelliti Amazon Leo che avrebbe dovuto portare in orbita. Il problema si è verificato circa dieci minuti dopo il decollo da Cape Canaveral, in Florida, quando il vettore aveva già superato le prime fasi dell'ascesa.

ULA ha confermato che il razzo non è riuscito a collocare il carico nell'orbita prevista, ma non ha ancora individuato la causa dell'anomalia. Siamo chiaramente in una fase confusa della vicenda, ma sappiamo che l'azienda ha avviato un'indagine per ricostruire la sequenza degli eventi e stabilire quali interventi saranno necessari prima di autorizzare un nuovo volo.

Dalle informazioni disponibili, i sei propulsori laterali a combustibile solido sembrano aver funzionato regolarmente,così come il primo stadio, che ha completato la parte iniziale dell'ascesa, sebbene i tempi osservati abbiano mostrato alcune differenze rispetto alla sequenza prevista.

items.title: Firefox 160 porta il Picture-in-Picture anche alle pagine web
items.summary: Firefox 160 introduce Mini Window per tenere pagine e sezioni web sempre in primo piano.
items.content:
Chi lavora con più schede aperte conosce bene il problema: stai scrivendo un documento, devi controllare continuamente una pagina di riferimento e finisci per passare da una finestra all'altra. Firefox ha introdotto una funzione che permette di tenere quella pagina sempre visibile, anche mentre si utilizzano altri programmi.

Si chiama Mini Window e fa parte delle novità di Firefox 160, ma come funziona? Sostanzialmente riprende il funzionamento del Picture-in-Picture, utilizzato da anni per guardare video in una finestra sovrapposta alle altre, ma lo estende alle normali pagine web. Ciò significa che si può mantenere in primo piano una chat, un documento, un modulo oppure un sito da consultare durante il lavoro.

Per utilizzarla basta aprire Firefox, fare clic con il pulsante destro sulla scheda interessata e scegliere Move Tab, quindi Move to Mini Window, a quel punto la pagina viene trasferita in una finestra compatta, indipendente da quella principale, che rimane visibile sopra le altre applicazioni.

items.title: Wife of assassinated ex-Haitian leader registers for presidential election
items.summary: There has not been an election in Haiti since before the death of Jovenel Moise in 2021.
items.content:
The widow of assassinated former Haitian president Jovenel Moise has registered as a presidential candidate for next year's elections in the Caribbean nation.

Martine Moise was injured in the gun attack that killed her husband at their home in the capital, Port-au-Prince, in 2021.

Haiti, which last held an election in 2016, has been plagued with chronic instability and gang violence.

Elections were scheduled to be held in December but were postponed last month until July due to the country's insecurity.

Moise has to comment on her candidacy but the electoral council website showed her registration on Sunday.

Last week she said on X: "Haiti will rise again on its own two feet, because politics needs to be done differently."

A total of 33 candidates have registered for the elections, including former presidents Michel Martelly and Jocelerme Privert, former prime minister Claude Joseph and former foreign minister Dominique Dupuy.

Jovenel Moise, who led Haiti from 2017 until his death, was shot dead at his home in Port-au-Prince in July 2021 , allegedly by a group of mainly Colombian mercenaries.

Martine Moise suffered serious gunshot wounds during the attack and was flown to a hospital in Florida.

She was charged in connection with the assassination in 2024, but the indictment was overturned last year.

The assassination shook the Caribbean nation to its core, with many Haitians shocked that the 53-year-old was killed with such apparent ease.

Thirty suspects have been indicted over the killing so far and in September 18 people were flown from Haiti to Florida to stand trial for their alleged involvement in the assassination.

Haiti has been engulfed in a wave of gang violence since the assassination of Moise.

At least 1,408 people were killed and 656 injured from April through to June this year, according to the UN Integrated Office in Haiti.

items.title: Why Berlusconi still holds sway in Italy
items.summary: The Cavaliere’s men still dominate football and television, while his political, cultural and business legacy lives on. Books about him keep coming, and the sale of his villa to the Al Thani family has made headlines worldwide. Yet his party is struggling
items.content:
ROME – When Silvio Berlusconi walked out of the doors of Palazzo Chigi for the last time in 2011, never to return as prime minister, he whispered a consoling prophecy to those around him: “Italians will miss me.” Nostalgia is a personal feeling, and a difficult one to measure. But in Italy in 2026, fifteen years after that distant autumn evening and just over three years after his death on 12 June 2023, the presence of the Cavaliere still looms large over the centre-right and beyond.

There are many signs of Berlusconi’s lingering presence, and rather than fading, they seem to be growing stronger with time. They extend beyond politics to the two spheres of influence on which Berlusconi built his two-decade dominance: football and television.

Take football. In mid-December, an assembly will be held to elect the next president of the powerful Italian Football Federation (FIGC). The strongest candidate, backed by the players’ and coaches’ associations, is a familiar face: 82-year-old Adriano Galliani, Berlusconi’s right-hand man since the late 1970s.

Galliani helped the founder build his private television empire before becoming chief executive of AC Milan during the club’s golden years, when it won eight Serie A titles and five Champions League trophies. He now enjoys a comfortable salary as a senator for Forza Italia, the party he helped his old friend found in 1994.

As for television, that is the domain of Berlusconi’s second son, Pier Silvio, chairman and chief executive of MFE – MediaForEurope, the international group that grew out of Mediaset, Italy’s leading private television broadcaster.

Berlusconi junior is plotting a return to France to avenge his father’s failure to conquer the French market with La Cinq, the country’s first private commercial television channel, launched in 1985 and later driven into bankruptcy, partly because of fierce resistance from France’s intellectual and political establishment.

“France would be the missing piece,” Pier Silvio Berlusconi confirmed on 11 November, responding to a question about the group’s future strategy.

Meanwhile, publishers continue to churn out books examining the Berlusconi phenomenon, confirming both the public’s enduring fascination and the Cavaliere’s lingering cultural influence.

In 2026 alone, five new books by different authors have appeared, ranging from Berlusconi Confidential by Marco Galluzzo, who covered his years in government as a journalist, to Il regista di Berlusconi, the memoir of Roberto Gasparotti, the man who masterminded the Forza Italia leader’s public image.

Berlusconi remains a political, cultural and business phenomenon, but also an enduring figure in Italian popular culture. Afternoon television shows spent days discussing the property deal of the year: the sale last June of the Cavaliere’s Sardinian paradise to Qatar’s ruling Al Thani family for €350 million.

Villa Certosa, the tycoon’s summer residence, with its collection of a thousand cacti, swimming pools, artificial volcano, secret mooring inside a cave, spa and, above all, its legendary bunga-bunga room, has become a permanent fixture in the Italian popular imagination, almosta fairy-tale world .

Berlusconi would have been delighted to learn that Jared Kushner, Donald Trump’s influential son-in-law, is considering reviving the Nato-Russia Council to bring the war in Ukraine to an end through a sweeping agreement that would reshape Europe’s security architecture.

It is precisely the diplomatic framework that the Cavaliere regarded as his greatest achievement, culminating in the 2002 handshake between Vladimir Putin and George W. Bush at the summit in Pratica di Mare, Italy.

Berlusconi never tired of talking about what he called “the spirit of Pratica di Mare”, which, he claimed, had brought the Cold War to an end.

The fate of Forza Italia, the political vehicle through which Berlusconi entered politics in 1994, looks rather less fortunate.

Under the leadership of Antonio Tajani, who also serves as Italy’s foreign minister, the party is stagnating and appears far from its stated goal of returning to more than 10 per cent of the vote.

Berlusconi’s eldest children continue to fund the party but prudently keep their distance from it. Rumours that his eldest daughter Marina, now head of Fininvest and the Mondadori publishing house, might stand for parliament are repeatedly denied.

“Neither my sister Marina nor I have any intention of entering active politics,” Pier Silvio Berlusconi said recently, putting an end to the speculation.

With polls placing Forza Italia at between 6 and 7 per cent, the party is struggling to find its voice within the centre-right, overshadowed by Giorgia Meloni’s dominant role.

An internal battle has erupted between the more liberal wing, which identifies with Marina Berlusconi, and the more conservative faction aligned with party secretary Antonio Tajani, who is accused of being excessively subservient to Meloni.

News of a secret lunch between Forza Italia minister Paolo Zangrillo and Francesca Pascale, Berlusconi’s partner for ten years and now an LGBTQ+ activist and outspoken critic of Tajani, has also caused a stir.

The Dottore’s last partner, Marta Fascina, now 36, has held a seat in the Chamber of Deputies for eight years, despite an absentee rate approaching 90 per cent of parliamentary sittings. She has, however, stayed out of the party’s internal power struggle.

And so, as the next election approaches, the Cavaliere’s political legacy appears to be fading away amid petty rivalries, a failure to renew the party, senior figures defecting to other parties and a lack of compelling proposals capable of reversing its decline.

It is further proof of a familiar rule: charismatic parties sooner or later burn out once their founder is gone.

This article was reviewed by an external translation partner

items.title: Shakespeare takes centre stage at Lecce’s Carlo V Castle
items.summary: A journey into the Bard’s world is captivating Salento from the underground chambers of Puglia’s largest fortress, with a possible extension until next spring.
items.content:
There is a place in Lecce where 16th-century walls seem to whisper the secrets of history’s greatest playwright, and where the boundaries between reality, illusion and madness dissolve into the darkness of underground chambers.

This is Carlo V Castle, originally built in the 12th century during the Norman period. Since last July, it has been hosting The Matter of Dreams: Worlds and Visions in Shakespeare’s Works.

The good news is that organisers are considering extending the exhibition until at least next spring. It was originally scheduled to close on January 10.

If, as Shakespeare famously wrote in The Tempest (Act IV, Scene I), “We are such stuff as dreams are made on”, then Lecce’s fortress – the largest castle in Puglia – is the perfect setting for an immersive journey into the Bard’s universe.

“The choice of this venue was by no means accidental,” explains Pietro Copani, director of Carlo V Castle. Lecce’s strong theatrical tradition further strengthens the connection between the exhibition and the city.

Conceived and created by Peter Bottazzi and Silvia Rigon, this original international project is promoted by the Swabian Castle of Bari, part of the Regional Directorate of National Museums of Puglia.

Bringing an undertaking of this scale to life took time. Two years were needed to conceive, develop and design the entire exhibition, bringing its multimedia elements together with the scholarly rigour ensured by Michael Dobson, director of the Shakespeare Institute in Stratford-upon-Avon, who served as an adviser to the project.

The exhibition unfolds through the castle’s atmospheric underground chambers and features seven major multimedia installations.

The journey begins with Prospero’s Ship, inspired by the central character in The Tempest and symbolically made up of all Shakespeare’s works. It is an immersive soundscape featuring poetic verses read in 40 languages.

Next comes the Shakespeare Workshop, an educational and documentary space exploring the playwright’s life and body of works.

Visitors then encounter Soliloquy, an intimate, multisensory environment built around Hamlet’s famous “To be or not to be” speech, inviting reflection on life’s great existential dilemmas.

The Fantastic transforms words into visual experiences through video mapping and songs from The Tempest, Macbeth, A Midsummer Night’s Dream and Hamlet.

The journey continues with Radio Shakespeare, an evocative soundscape exploring the power of listening, voice and theatrical memory, and Through Words, where pages and verses seem to dissolve into light across the castle’s stone walls, tracing the transmission of literary heritage through time.

The final installation, Between the Cracks of Power, revisits the dramatic tensions, conspiracies and betrayals typical of Shakespeare’s history plays.

“Rather than simply telling Shakespeare’s story, we wanted to convey his extraordinary ability to inspire new questions, interpretations and forms of imagination, even today,” explain curators Bottazzi and Rigon.

“The collaboration with the Shakespeare Institute and the interdisciplinary nature of this initiative reflect our commitment to developing projects with an international outlook, bringing places of outstanding historical value into dialogue with new forms of storytelling and public engagement,” says Anita Guarnieri, director of the Swabian Castle of Bari and the Regional Directorate of National Museums of Puglia.

Maria d’Enghien, Countess of Lecce and later Queen of Naples, ruled the city and chose the castle as her permanent residence from 1420 until her death in 1446.

The fortress underwent its most significant transformation between 1537 and 1550, on the orders of Holy Roman Emperor Charles V of Habsburg. To defend against Ottoman invasions, the old medieval structure was incorporated into an Italian-style fortress with imposing angular bastions, designed by military engineer Giangiacomo dell’Acaya.

Over the centuries, the castle has served many purposes: a barracks, a courthouse and a military district, before eventually being returned to the city as a cultural centre.

Hidden beneath the medieval Torre Mozza, the castle’s underground chambers contain one of its most evocative areas: the old prisons. They hold stories of human tragedy and extraordinary twists of fate. Among those who died here in extreme poverty was Giangiacomo dell’Acaya himself, the very architect who had designed and built the fortress.

The royal engineer was imprisoned within the walls he had conceived after falling into financial ruin when he acted as guarantor for a debtor who defaulted on his obligations. Over the years, the cells also held prominent figures from Salento’s intellectual and cultural circles, including the thinker Vittorio Prioli.

A visit to the exhibition is best combined with a guided tour of the fortress, which takes in the historic prisons, covered in graffiti, the Maria d’Enghien Hall and the Papier-mâché Museum.

Housed in the castle’s former stables, the museum is a unique gem showcasing around 80 masterpieces of Salento’s traditional papier-mâché craft, which dates back to the 18th century. Many depict sacred figures once carried through the streets in religious processions.

Carlo V Castle is open Tuesday to Sunday, from 10 am to 8 pm.

Castle guided tour and admission to the on-site museums: €10.

For further information and bookings, visit www.ilcastellodilecce.it .

items.title: Swap goods or skills for a stay: Italy's Barter Week is back
items.summary: Photography, gardening, vintage finds, olive oil and wine: an initiative by Bed-and-Breakfast.it, running from 16 to 22 November, invites travellers to discover a different approach to travel and accommodation
items.content:
A 120-bass accordion, for instance. Or a vintage advertising sign, a few bobbin-lace-making lessons, or even a project to bring bees back to an old garden.

This is not a list of unusual purchases: it is the wish list drawn up by Italian B&B hosts taking part in Barter Week, which runs from 16 to 22 November 2026.

The initiative, launched by Bed-and-Breakfast.it and now in its 18th edition, is based on a simple idea: enjoy a stay without money changing hands, offering something in return that might prove useful or interesting to your host.

You don't necessarily need valuable possessions or extraordinary talents to take part. A skill, a passion, a few hours of work or a product from your home region can all serve as currency.

The possibilities range from photography and gardening to maintenance work, website design, computer lessons and help with managing social media accounts.

Among the most common requests are extra-virgin olive oil, wine, cheese and local food specialities. Some hosts even suggest swapping hospitality itself: a few nights at their own B&B in exchange for a stay at another property, perhaps in a region they have yet to discover.

But it is the initiative's online wish list that really brings out the more unusual side of the project. And there is no shortage of ideas to suit every taste.

Relais Accademia, for example, is looking for a vintage advertising sign, either enamelled or neon. Flower Bed & Breakfast, meanwhile, is offering a stay in exchange for a 120-bass accordion.

Ma Che Idea would love to find someone willing to teach its hosts the traditional art of bobbin lace-making, while La Finestra sul Giardino is on the lookout for an illustrator to create a children's book.

In Puglia, at Masseria Murgia Albanese, bartering can even turn into a small environmental project. The aim is to restore a bee-friendly garden of around 500 square metres surrounding an eighteenth-century apiary, to attract bees again.

Further south, in Salento, Giardino Frannicola is looking for artists willing to help create an open-air gallery, with works inspired by local history and traditions. Elsewhere, the requests include old books and magazines published between 1968 and 1977, or a stone laundry basin that can be restored and repurposed as a decorative feature on a terrace.

Behind these seemingly disparate requests lies a vision of hospitality that goes beyond simply providing a bed for the night.

For B&B hosts, bartering can be a way to meet a practical need, bring a shelved project to life or connect with people who share their interests.

For travellers, it offers the chance to build a relationship with a place and the people who live there, contributing something of their own rather than simply paying for a room. After all, the value of an exchange cannot be measured in money alone.

Taking part is straightforward: visitors to the initiative's website can search for participating B&Bs by destination or browse the Wish List.

Once they have found a property, they simply contact the host directly to suggest an exchange, either by responding to an existing request or putting forward an idea of their own. The length of the stay and the terms of the arrangement are agreed between the two parties.

Although the event officially runs from 16 to 22 November, some participating properties are happy to arrange barter stays throughout the year.

After all, sometimes you don't need a credit card to travel: just something to offer.

items.title: Alessandro Carloni: “I drew inspiration from Roberto Benigni for my ‘Cat in the Hat’”
items.summary: The animated film co-directed by the Italian filmmaker has grossed $20 million in the US, putting it second at the box office behind Godzilla Minus Zero
items.content:
Rome – “In America, the Cat in the Hat is a bit like Pinocchio in Italy,” says Alessandro Carloni, the Bologna-born director who has made his mark in Hollywood with Kung Fu Panda and How to Train Your Dragon. He is talking about Warner Bros.’ animated film, which he co-directed with Erica Rivinoja.

On its opening weekend, the Cat in the Hat found itself chasing a monster at the box office: the film took $20 million in the US, $10 million less than Godzilla Minus Zero. In Italy, where the Japanese film opened on 12 November, The Cat in the Hat has grossed €1 million – not a bad result, considering the character created by Dr Seuss has historically struggled to find success on the big screen.

“I was developing three films for Netflix, one of them with Paul McCartney. Then there was a change in leadership, and 25 projects were cancelled. Meanwhile, Warner Bros. had acquired the rights to the Cat in the Hat and approached Erica Rivinoja and me.”

“In the book, the children are bored, indecisive and frightened at the beginning. By the end, they have become more self-confident. I saw the Cat as a clown, or a kind of psychologist – an emotional support animal.”

“Yes. My mother has Alzheimer’s, and I'm gradually saying goodbye to her. Meanwhile, I've had a little girl of my own and watched my wife become a mother. Becoming a parent changes your identity. I used to be an illustrator, a writer, a director. Now I'm a dad.”

How do you strike the right balance between comedy and tears?

“When I was a child, I watched Back to the Future. At the end, when the photograph of the siblings reappears, I cried. Not even a drama had ever moved me that much. If you can make someone laugh, they're more open to being moved afterwards.”

“When I first met my wife, she had to go to the police headquarters to sort out some paperwork. It was mind-numbingly boring. But I was so in love with her that I thought it was wonderful just to go along. It's the same with a character: if you love them, you want to spend time with them, whatever they're doing.”

“During the first screenings, Po came across as obnoxious, convinced he was amazing. Then we turned him into a lovable softie who adores kung fu, and audiences fell in love with him.”

“He may seem like a bit of a charlatan, but everything he does is out of love. He wants to help the children. And he succeeds.”

“Yes. His characters always seem like children trapped inside grown-ups. I dream of creating a new mythology: whenever a child feels sad, the Cat comes along to cheer them up, just like Father Christmas.”

“My father was an illustrator and worked at Gamma Film in the 1950s. He loved abstraction and taught me to simplify images to make them more emotionally powerful. We've eliminated shadows and reflections. It's made on a computer, but it looks hand-drawn.”

“I love characters who exist in silence, who communicate through their eyes. In American cinema, dialogue is written for the audience; in Italian cinema, there's more spontaneity. I left Italy when I was 17, but that sensibility has stayed with me.”

“The ones featuring the ‘Things’. We had no idea what to do with them at first. Then we came up with a language built around rhythm and melody. For two weeks, I drew storyboards and recorded handclaps. When we showed our work to the studio, everyone burst out laughing.”

“I wrote it into the film as a joke, but I really hope it happens.”

items.title: Stop Filming in Log
items.summary: Article URL: https://digitalfilms.wordpress.com/2026/11/15/stop-filming-in-log/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50514093 Points: 27 # Comments: 16
items.content:
I may ruffle some feathers with that title; but after years as a colorist, log-encoded clips can be an unnecessary challenge. Using camera log profiles is often a crutch for location and studio set-ups. Or it’s simply used because the internet tells you log = film. That’s just not true. Many times a videographer will shoot log incorrectly – generally underexposed – expecting to ‘fix it in post’. The same issues apply to shooting in camera raw or HDR.

In the video world, camera raw was introduced by the RED Digital Cinema Camera Company in 2007, borrowing from still photo concepts. Log (logarithmic) videography came to the forefront when ARRI introduced the Alexa in 2010 , which offered a Log-C profile. ARRI’s camera raw format wasn’t post-friendly, so Log-C was a better fit. The goal of both manufacturers was to shoot video with a wide dynamic range that could be recovered and adjusted in post production. Other camera manufacturers followed suit, including even Apple and its iPhones.

The earliest digital films were shot using Sony F900 (modified by Panavision) and Thomson Viper FilmStream cameras . These gave us films like Attack of the Clones , Collateral , Zodiac , and Benjamin Button . The Sony image was basically a standard Rec. 709 profile, whereas the Viper used a different color science. While the image wasn’t log or raw as we know it today, it did generate a green cast that had to be corrected in the color grade.

In reality, film doesn’t have an equivalent to log or raw. Motion picture film negative is typically shot with proper exposure and then color corrected when going to print. A film timer does the color correction, but the tools and looks are nowhere near as surgical as modern video color correction. While film negative might be scanned in the Cineon color space, this isn’t exactly the same as video log. If the film was transferred using some type of film scanner ( like the modern Cintel Scanner from Blackmagic Design ), then the result will be an image that’s close to standard or HDR video.

The Alexa’s introduction created many copy-cat cameras that each used different color profiles in log. These all required different LUTs (color look-up tables) to get you back to a Rec. 709 image. Quite frankly, I haven’t been too happy with the majority of these. The ARRI and Panasonic implementations look pretty good to me. Everyone else? Not so much.

Unfortunately, Sony made things even more confusing by introducing various profiles, including camera raw, s709, several iterations of S-Log, S-Cinetone, and, of course, Rec. 709. I’ve worked various projects shot in S-Log and it’s always a toss-up whether or not you can grade a good-looking image from the footage. Of these options, I like S-Cinetone the best . It can make a wonderful image .

From the WhoIsMatt website , “According to Sony, the base S-Cinetone curve is Rec. 709, but adds some filmic qualities. It has high contrast tone in low luminance levels and low contrast tone in the high luminance levels. The black level is lower than s709 and Rec. 709. With a low highlight contrast, S-Cinetone will have softer and lighter highlights, but higher contrast levels in low luminance levels will give you a more saturated look.”

This brings us to camera raw. Most users will only deal with camera raw from either RED or Blackmagic Design cameras . Each take different approaches, which have evolved over time. While camera raw can be useful in post, it’s not essential. If you shoot correctly with 709 in mind, then the raw result will fall right into line and be easily correctable, even if you don’t adjust the raw settings.

I’ll wrap this up with HDR (high dynamic range). Understand that HDR video is not the same thing as HDR photography. They use different science and apply different technology to the sensor image. HDR video is based largely on Dolby and Canon’s push to sell more display systems.

Many cameras can shoot in an HDR mode, which provides a peak brightness that far exceeds Rec. 709. However, in spite of all the marketing that tells you HDR is the image your eyes see, that simply isn’t true. Assume that you are in a dark room with bright sunlight visible through a window at the far end. Your eyes do not see all the information in the dark corners of the room and at the same time all the puffy clouds in the blue sky outside. Your eye ‘stops down’ for the window, or opens up for the room detail, making the window painful to look at. Yet, HDR videography and display systems reproduce exactly that. The result is a very painful-to-watch image on the display device. RED actually tried to approach HDR capture like a still photo camera, but their solution never caught on .

Smart phone cameras have become HDR-video-capable, even though most users have no idea what it is or how to set it correctly. Hence, you occasionally see an HDR video pop up on someone’s YouTube channel, making in nearly impossible to watch in a dim room. Also, in spite of the efforts of Canon and Dolby, true HDR has really not taken hold more broadly. Yes, there are camera and displays capable of some level of HDR – and yes, some streaming services, such as Netflix and YouTube, support it. But, it really is not a factor in the large amount of content that’s created globally.

Add to this feature films. There is a theatrical version of HDR, but it’s not nearly at the extreme levels of video HDR. Few if any films that I’ve seen use it. Whether or not HDR will be more of a factor in the future is an unknown. Nevertheless, in the context of this blog post, don’t shoot anything in a video HDR mode unless you specifically have been tasked to deliver HDR content.

Boiling this down: shooting in some version of Rec. 709, especially if it’s correctly lit and uses a low-contrast profile, will often yield much better results. Dealing with these clips will be easier in post than all the other recommendations that the internet puts in front of you.

items.title: Watch: New York teen reunites with cat missing after building collapse
items.summary: Rescuers found the pet cat in the ruins of Zariah's apartment four days after she made an emotional plea to the public.
items.content:
A teenage girl and her cat have been reunited four days after a building in the New York borough of Brooklyn collapsed.

Zariah Coleman, 13, made an emotional plea when her pet went missing after she and her family were forced to relocate when the side of their building was stripped off in the unexpected collapse.

City officials later found her cat, Isaac, in the debris of the their home and shared the reunion on Sunday afternoon.

Eight people died and 18 others were injured when the three-storey building collapsed in the Flatbush neighbourhood last Wednesday.

items.title: Il principe Harry partecipa agli Invictus Games dell'Ucraina a Leopoli
items.summary: Applaudito dai militari feriti ai quali ha detto: 'Vincerete la guerra'
items.content:
Il principe Harry ha partecipato agli Invictus Games panucraini a Leopoli e ha mostrato il suo sostegno ai difensori dell'Ucraina. Secondo quanto riportato da Ukrinform , Maksym Kozytskyi, capo dell'amministrazione militare regionale di Leopoli, lo ha comunicato tramite Telegram .

"Il principe Harry ha visitato gli Invictus Games di tutta l'Ucraina a Leopoli! Ha sostenuto personalmente i nostri atleti durante la competizione di rugby in carrozzina", ha scritto il governatore regionale.

Kozytskyi ha sottolineato che la visita è stata particolarmente toccante perché il principe Harry ha fondato gli Invictus Games nel 2014. Si sono vissute scene commoventi quando è stato applaudito dai militari feriti a Leopoli, dove ha detto al pubblico: "Vincerete la guerra", come ha riportato la Bbc.

Secondo Kozytskyi, circa 500 partecipanti provenienti da tutta l'Ucraina si sono iscritti quest'anno agli Invictus Games panucraini di Leopoli. In base ai risultati della competizione, verrà selezionata una squadra di 60 veterani e militari che rappresenterà l'Ucraina agli Invictus Games internazionali di Birmingham nel 2027.

In Ucraina ci sono più di 150.000 veterani di guerra feriti e il principe ha visitato progetti a sostegno della loro cura e riabilitazione.

items.title: Mexican drug lord Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo dies age 80
items.summary: Known as the 'Boss of Bosses', he was the head of all-powerful Guadalajara Cartel in the 1980s before his arrest broke up his drug organisation.
items.content:
Notorious Mexican drug lord Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo has died in hospital aged 80.

Félix Gallardo was widely considered one of the biggest drug smugglers in history and is credited with building an alliance between criminal groups in Colombia and his own Mexican cartel.

Known as The Godfather or the "Boss of Bosses", Félix Gallardo was the head of the all-powerful Guadalajara Cartel, which reigned over Mexican drug trafficking at the height of the cocaine boom of the 1980s.

At the time, it created a new modus operandi in the illegal drug trade which endures to this day. He had been in state custody since 1989.

The name Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo will echo through the annals of drug-trafficking history more than any other except perhaps Pablo Escobar's.

He led the organisation which revolutionised drug smuggling in the region by entering into partnership with the Colombian cartels, particularly Escobar's Medellín Cartel, to combine production in the Andes with Mexican transportation across the border into the United States.

At one point an estimated 80% of all cocaine that entered the US came from the Medellín Cartel. Félix Gallardo and his organisation played a major role in smuggling it in.

At its height, the Guadalajara Cartel under Félix Gallardo exerted huge influence over Mexican politics and law enforcement, controlling entire police networks and state governorships.

In 1985, the net started to tighten around the leaders of the cartel following the torture and murder of a DEA agent, Enrique "Kiki" Camarena.

Camarena had angered them after he had discovered and then destroyed a vast marijuana plantation in Chihuahua, which belonged to the criminal group.

His murder sparked one of the biggest manhunts the US government has ever launched in North America.

In 1989, Félix Gallardo was captured and sentenced to decades in prison. In ill health, he was granted house arrest in 2022 but technical problems with electronic ankle monitoring prevented his transfer. He died in hospital in his native Guadalajara.

In the 1980s, Joaquin "El Chapo" Guzmán was introduced to Félix Gallardo, who put him in charge of handling logistics for his drug organisation.

From the subsequent break-up of Félix Gallardo's organisation after his arrest, the Sinaloa Cartel emerged, led by Guzmán, now another man synonymous with large-scale drug trafficking.

In 2019, Guzmán was sentenced to life in prison for charges including drug trafficking and money laundering following one of the most high-profile trials in recent US history.

Félix Gallardo's life has been portrayed in a number of television programmes including the Netflix series Narcos: Mexico. The show depicted his rise to power as well as his relationship with Guzmán.

items.title: Australian MP 'full of gratitude' upon leaving hospital after alleged car attack
items.summary: The MP lost both of her legs after the alleged attack outside her electorate office four weeks ago.
items.content:
Australian politician Helen Haines has said she is "full of gratitude" upon being discharged from hospital, four weeks after she was allegedly attacked with a car and left a double amputee.

The independent MP was struck outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, north-east of Melbourne, on October 19, an incident which horrified Australia.

Brendan Nugent, 43, has been charged with dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury and the federal offence of causing harm to a public official. He has yet to enter pleas.

In her first public comments since the attack, Haines, 65, said she had moved into the rehabilitation stage of her recovery.

"This is a really positive moment, and I am full of gratitude for the expert and compassionate care I received at the Alfred and am receiving in this next stage," Haines said.

"I appreciate the thousands of warm wishes and supportive messages from people across Indi, throughout Australia and around the world. They are giving me strength as I focus on this next phase of healing."

She added that she had been "overwhelmed" by the generosity of well wishers who had donated to Save the Children in her honour.

Haines, known for supporting stronger climate action and helping establish a national anti-corruption commission, entered parliament in 2019 as the Member for Indi after working as a nurse and midwife.

Victoria Police has said its investigation, with support from the Australian Federal Police, remains ongoing and a motive is yet to be established.

Nugent's father said he and his wife had been long-time friends of Haines, and Nugent's lawyer has said his client has mental health concerns.

The incident sparked a reckoning in the country more broadly over the tone of public debate.

Though a motive is still unclear, politicians, law enforcement, and experts have said heated public discourse is heightening the threat of political violence in the country.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said he had been in regular contact with Haines and her "extraordinary" family.

"All our thoughts and prayers continue to be with Helen for her recovery," he said in a statement.

"We continue to provide support to Helen, her family, community and staff as she undertakes her rehabilitation."

'Targeted' attack on much-loved MP leaves Australian town heartbroken

items.title: Yemeni forces' retreat leaves Houthis in control of key Red Sea waterway
items.summary: Saudi-backed forces say they are moving troops from the Bab al-Mandab Strait to defend the interim capital Aden.
items.content:
Yemeni pro-government forces backed by Saudi Arabia have said they are withdrawing from an area overlooking the strategically important Bab al-Mandab Strait, leaving it under the control of the Iran-backed Houthi movement.

Yemen's military said it was redeploying troops from the key shipping gateway at the southern end of the Red Sea to defend its interim capital, Aden.

The shift ends a weeks-long offensive to try to secure the area near the waterway after the Houthis seized it in a surprise offensive in September, squeezing global oil exports and prompting thousands to flee.

Houthi-run media reported later on Sunday the group had taken control of the territory. Saudi Arabia has not commented.

Pro-government forces said they had "secured" the strait in early October as they sought to retake crucial ground from the Houthis, who said they had captured areas including Perim Island at the mouth of the strait and the strategic port city of Mokha a month prior.

But the Saudi-backed forces fighting on behalf of Yemen's internationally recognised government said on Sunday they were withdrawing to reinforce troops elsewhere, with the southern city of Aden a "priority".

The Reuters news agency reported a Southern Armed Forces statement which said troops were being withdrawn "from Dhubab Airport and the Bab al-Mandab area".

It said the decision had been made with the aim of "strengthening the front lines and addressing existing threats".

The Houthis said they posed no threat to international shipping passing through the waterway when they captured it, but that they would continue to target vessels from Saudi Arabia.

However, the seizure contributed to a surge in global oil prices because Saudi Arabia had been relying on the Red Sea for oil exports since the US and Israel's war with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz.

Saudi Arabia responded with hundreds of air strikes, while the Houthis launched hundreds of drones and missiles at its cities and infrastructure.

The UN has estimated that nearly 330,000 people have been displaced in Yemen as the fighting has since escalated. Hundreds of people are reported to have been killed.

Yemenis flee across Red Sea as Houthis and Saudi-backed forces escalate war

Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from its capital Sanaa.

The conflict escalated in 2015, after a Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.

A four-year informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.

The Houthis said they were retaliating for a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom.

items.title: Pechino conferma il trilaterale tra Xi, Trump e Putin e gli Usa si blindano sull'IA contro la Cina
items.summary: Gli Stati Uniti ei suoi alleati hanno concordato di creare un elenco congiunto di tecnologie e supply chain dell'IA che necessitano di più protezione
items.content:
La Cina conferma un vertice trilaterale tra il presidente Xi Jinping e i suoi omologhi lo statunitense e russo, Donald Trump e il russo Vladimir Putin per giovedì 19 novembre a Shenzhen. Lo ha reso noto il Ministero degli Affari Esteri cinese. Non è stato specificato quali saranno i temi al centro dell'incontro. L'evento dovrebbe svolgersi a margine del vertice dei leader dell'APEC.

Intanto gli Usa e i loro alleati, tra cui Giappone, Australia, Israele e Gb, hanno concordato di creare un elenco congiunto di tecnologie e supply chain dell'IA che necessitano di più protezione, nell'ottica di contrasto della Cina . Jacob Helberg, sottosegretario di Stato americano agli affari economici, ha detto al Financial Times che anche Corea del Sud, India, Qatar ed Emirati Arabi Uniti hanno firmato la 'Dichiarazione di San Francisco sulle basi sicure per una prosperità duratura', mentre Germania, Svezia, Olanda e Ue lo faranno la prossima settimana. Donald Trump incontrerà giovedì Xi Jinping, a margine del forum dell'Apec di Shenzhen.

items.title: Universal XSS in uBlock Origin from website-driven element picker
items.summary: Article URL: https://iter.ca/post/ubo-uxss/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50513160 Points: 268 # Comments: 68
items.content:
Earlier this month I found a one-click universal XSS issue with uBlock Origin (the MV2 Firefox version, although a similar but less problematic issue also affected the MV3 version, uBO Lite), where a malicious website could trick the extension into adding arbitrary trusted filters. Trusted filters can inject JavaScript code into pages, and so the malicious website could create a trusted filter on another website and run arbitrary JS in the context of any site. This issue is fixed now; you can read the GitHub advisory for some more details.

GPT-5.6 Sol did most of the hard work of finding the issue. I figured there might be some kind of UXSS from filter injection, so I asked it to take a look, and it found the issue. I then checked and verified the issue it proposed. I wrote all of the prose in this post myself; Claude wrote most of the code for the PoC.

uBlock Origin has an element picker that you can pull up by right-clicking on the page. You can use this to create a filter rule to block an element on the page without leaving the page.

The element picker is implemented by injecting an iframe to a URL like moz-extension://76b2331a-894c-4d25-8b89-fcce37e79cc4/web_accessible_resources/epicker-ui.html . That page can talk to the extension background script and tell it to add filters.

On Firefox, the only information we needed to figure out was the extension internal UUID which is random per-installation.

On the default setup uBO has a lootdest.*##+js(no-fetch-if, adsbygoogle, war:googlesyndication_adsbygoogle.js) filter rule (from uAssets), which hooks fetch . From inside the fetch hook, it makes an XHR request to moz-extension:// /web_accessible_resources/googlesyndication_adsbygoogle.js and returns the response from that as the fetch body, instead of actually making the request. The filter rule is intended to replace a network request for JS from an ad server with a dummy script that has the correct API but doesn't do anything.

But the attacker website can itself hook the XHR made from inside the no-fetch-if hook to extract the random extension UUID.

Then the attacker website can run fetch('/adsbygoogle.js').catch(() => {}); to trigger the filter, and make their hooked XHR run. Note that there are several ways that the extension internal UUID could be leaked; it's not just this one filter rule.

Then you can use that to iframe the element picker. Given an iframe element in the page, you just set its src to `moz-extension://${origin}/web_accessible_resources/epicker-ui.html` .

Now we can drive the element picker. We can create a MessageChannel and do iframe.contentWindow.postMessage({ what: 'epickerStart' }, '*', [ch.port2]); to send it to the picker iframe. Then we talk to it: it sends us a start message, we send it a showDialog message with a filter and a resultsetDetails message 1 to enable the create button and set opt .

Normally the picker restricts what filters you can enter, and doesn't let you add scriptlet filters. But there's a trick we can do to add arbitrary filters. There's an opt field we set in the second message which is normally the type of network request to match (like image ), and gets appended to the filter with a $ if set, like $image . But since we control it, we can put a newline in it and make it "image\ngoogle.com##+js(trusted-rpnt, script, ...)" to inject an arbitrary trusted filter that injects a script. 2

This is where the main issue is - the element picker shouldn't accept messages from the attacker. One of the fixes was having a secret password that the real element picker gets from the content script, that the element picker sends in the initial postMessage.

I didn't bother actually implementing this, but malicious websites could overlay stuff on top of the embedded element picker or make it invisible by setting the iframe opacity to 0. So as long as the website can get the user to click on the page, it can add arbitrary trusted filters for arbitrary domains.

Filters added by the element picker are always treated as trusted (at least until a recompile), which is why it can add a trusted filter. If the user later changes their custom filters it would cause a recompile, clearing the filter trust. But in practice the attacker could just immediately open the victim webpage, so this doesn't help much.

Originally I sent that message in reply to a dialogSetFilter message from the picker, but it turns out you can just send it right away instead of waiting to reply. ↩︎

items.title: Suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's ex-boss left in 2025, Megaspeed says
items.summary: The Nvidia scandal has raised questions over whether advanced AI chips ended up in China, despite US restrictions.
items.content:
Alice Huang, a suspected China spy who has been linked to Nvidia's former boss Jensen Huang, left her executive role at Megaspeed in August last year, the company says.

Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of the AI chip-making giant Nvidia after it emerged he had allegedly had affairs with Alice Huang as well as with one of his employees.

Megaspeed is the biggest buyer of Nvidia chips in South East Asia and the scandal at Nvidia has raised questions about the possibility that high-end AI chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions.

The Singapore-based company said on Sunday it had launched an internal investigation into its business.

Megaspeed said it was aware of reports "containing assertions about our business, supply chain and global operations that are not supported by verifiable evidence".

It added that it "conducts legitimate and lawful business" and has "retained external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation".

But while Alice Huang is said to have stepped down from her role as Megaspeed director near the end of 2023, there were suspicions that she was still heavily involved in the firm's operations, according to Washington-based security analysis group C4ADS

C4ADS said that Huang was still "practically in control" of Megaspeed even after she had handed over the reins of the firm.

Huang - who is of no relation to Nvidia's former boss - had been investigated by Singapore authorities in February 2025 as part of the country's probe into Megaspeed and other companies.

Also on Sunday, US Congressman John Moolenaar said that Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before the Select Committee on China, which he chairs, as well as the House Foreign Affairs and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence.

The committee heads had threatened to issue subpoenas to Huang if he did not comply with their requests to testify.

Moolenaar told CBS, BBC's US partner, that none were ultimately issued. Huang's testimony is expected to take place behind close doors, with the dates still being finalised.

"That's going to be a very important meeting to understand to what degree privileged information was accessed, and to what degree this potential alleged Chinese spy influenced Nvidia's philosophy and may have had an influence on some of our policies with respect to AI and export controls," the congressman told the Face The Nation programme.

Separately, a group of tech leaders, including Space X's Elon Musk, have been trying to rally support to have Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO.

A representative for Huang declined to comment on a report in the Financial Times Sunday suggesting that he was discussing a comeback to the firm he co-founded.

The BBC understands that the likelihood of Huang being reinstated to lead Nvidia is very low while the company's internal investigations are ongoing.

The move would also face scrutiny from Washington, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent calling for Nvidia to hire its next CEO from outside the company.

On Friday, Bessent had blamed fellow Trump cabinet colleague Howard Lutnick's commerce department for failing to properly oversee the export of high-end chips.

Bessent told CNBC that several agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months... but Commerce has the pen... and you will have to ask them about their internal process".

The so-called entity list restricts US trade with overseas firms and individuals.

Lutnick has been called to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month over his department's role in allowing Nvidia to export its advanced chips.

Other congressional committees have asked both Lutnick and his department to retain all records relating to Nvidia and Jensen Huang.

Megaspeed is suspected of giving backdoor access to Nvidia chips to Chinese companies via its data centres in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.

Nvidia has been banned from selling its advanced semiconductors to China.

While Singapore does not prohibit the transfer of advanced AI chips to companies abroad, such moves can breach US export controls.

Singapore has said that while it does not enforce "unilateral export controls imposed by other countries" it expects all companies in its jurisdiction to respect such regulations.

Megaspeed said it "designs and maintains its global operational and supply-chain control frameworks to comply with all applicable laws and regulatory regimes". It said this includes "US export control requirements and local jurisdiction rules in every market where we operate".

China has denied that Alice Huang is a spy and warned the US not to use the scandal as a "pretext for imposing a technological blockade" on AI technology.

Today, we are releasing 0.4.9.17 , which includes a series of security fixes. One fix in particular is especially important for relay DoS defenses related to IPv6 handling.

This release comes in rapid response to the ongoing DDoS attack on the network, which has affected most relay operators. This is not an easy problem to address, as relays across the network are being overwhelmed by a massive flood of client circuits. We are actively evaluating additional defenses and so expect further releases in the near future.

We want to extend a huge thank you to all relay operators who have been helping us deal with this ongoing attack. The tor-relays@ mailing list has been very active and we are very grateful for your time, effort, and support. Please, continue doing so!

If you run a relay, please upgrade as soon as possible. No action item is required after upgrading.

items.title: Russia's mega-rich are already imagining a future after Putin
items.summary: Some Russian tycoons are pining after a return to a 1990s system of oligarchy, when businessmen enjoyed power
items.content:
Hours after launching his full-scale invasion of Ukraine on 24 February 2022, Vladimir Putin gathered Russia's richest men in the Kremlin's cavernous Yekaterininsky Hall.

More than three dozen of them sat huddled along a wall, wearing face masks because of the Covid pandemic. One Russian newspaper reporter described them as "pale and sleep-deprived". On entering, Putin sat down at the opposite side of the hall, creating a vast space between him and the businessmen. As usual, he was wearing no mask.

Using his typically coded language, he said he expected them to support the war.

"I would like to call on you to show understanding of what is going on," he said, "and work together with the government to find the tools which would support production, the economy, jobs."

In the Kremlin-published video of the meeting, none of the invited billionaires said a word.

That silence has become a feature of the Russian super-rich. Over the decades of Putin's rule, they have learnt that the price of piping up could be high. In 2003, oil magnate Mikhail Khodorkovsky, Russia's richest man at the time, who was funding a number of opposition groups, accused Putin of presiding over rampant corruption. He spent the next 10 years behind bars, convicted of tax evasion, fraud and embezzlement - a warning to other would-be critics. He denied the charges.

And even if any of the tycoons objected to the war, they have tended to keep their thoughts to themselves.

But even in that silence, there are murmurings: some members of Russia's once-mighty business elite seem to be imagining a Russia after Putin. They are wondering if, once the president has left office or died, the country might look more like it did in the 1990s, when the oligarchs enjoyed the fruits of power - or even if a healthier politics may take root.

The journalist Arkady Ostrovsky, a prominent Kremlin-watcher at The Economist newspaper who recently spent hours interviewing one of Russia's richest men, says he feels that a "historic, political shift is happening" in terms of how the ultra-rich view the future of the country.

The collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991 gave birth to a new, powerful force on the domestic scene: people who took advantage of the end of communism and became extraordinarily rich, and then wanted to control politicians for their own benefit. They were dubbed "the oligarchs", from Ancient Greek for the "few who rule". They had money, which back then meant power.

This era of the "wild 1990s" was when the so-called "new Russians" burst onto the scene. Huge state companies came up for grabs, and men with the right connections became millionaires - even billionaires - almost overnight. Corruption was rife, cronyism rampant, and contract killings frequent.

But almost immediately after Putin was first elected as president in 2000, he subjugated the oligarchs. He had little interest in sharing power with anyone else. He could afford to stand up to the billionaires because Russia's economy was getting back on its feet, and the central government was getting stronger.

Bill Browder, a financier who used to be the biggest foreign investor in Russia, and was banned from the country in 2005 after campaigning against corruption, says the Russian tycoons cowered and wilted in front of Putin - for example at the Davos economic forum, in the pre-war years when they were still welcomed there.

"I can remember seeing oligarchs walking around like they own the place, the most arrogant and self-confident individuals. And then Putin showed up, and it was just remarkable to see how these supposedly alpha-male-on-steroids individuals turned into absolutely subordinate, almost desperate schoolchildren," he tells the BBC.

Since the outbreak of war in 2022, the Kremlin has kept Russia's rich businessmen in line with a ruthless policy of carrot and stick. Critics of the war have seen their assets seized, while loyalists have been rewarded with lavish government war contracts: today there are more Russian billionaires than ever (155 in total, according to Forbes magazine). Their collective wealth has reached a new high of nearly $700bn (£525bn).

But even for those tycoons who have stayed loyal and been rewarded, all of that money doesn't seem to be making them happy. Some are growing restless.

Their billions do not go as far as they used to: domestically, they cannot buy much political influence.

"They have no cards, they have no game," exiled politician and analyst Dmitry Nekrasov says. "They're rich because they've got something to do with Putin, not the other way round."

And outside of Russia, they are ostracised because of the Western sanctions imposed on Russia after its full-scale invasion.

"They're treated like low-level criminals. They can't fly their private jets. Their yachts can't park in all the best harbours in Europe. It must be very awful and humiliating for them," says Browder, the avowed Putin critic.

And so, quietly, some of their minds are turning to what happens after Putin leaves the scene. That's what I'm told by well-placed analysts, who are immersed in the world of these tycoons.

There's no immediate prospect of the president's departure, and there's no reason to think he's in bad health. But Putin, who turned 74 last month, has served in the Kremlin for a quarter of a century; people in Moscow know that his exit will come one day. When asked by Reuters last year if he intends to serve until 2036, when his constitutional term technically ends, Putin replied: "Only God knows if we have enough health."

If Putin resigned or died in office, the prime minister, Mikhail Mishustin, would take over. But Mishustin has not exhibited any presidential ambitions (that's probably a key reason he was appointed). That would create something of a power vacuum.

In that scenario, Russia-watchers I have spoken with envisage a few potential scenarios.

Some in the West, and no doubt within Russia, hope that democracy might flourish in a post-Putin Russia, with government led by the people, rather than by a new cadre of oligarchs or a single autocrat. But this seems like the least likely path, analysts say. Key democratic institutions have been eroded or destroyed over Putin's rule. "Russia is so used to violence, it has grown unaccustomed to standard democratic procedures," says Alexandra Prokopenko, an exiled Russian journalist and analyst.

Another path is more autocracy. A different figure could replace Putin and continue his culture of repression. But Prokopenko thinks this wouldn't be another strongman dictatorship - at least not right away. These things take time, she says: at first, Putin's successor would be weaker than him, with fewer resources.

And then there's the third option: tycoons re-assert their power and Russia returns to something resembling a 1990s-style system of oligarchy. Dmitry Nekrasov, a former Kremlin adviser and opposition politician who now lives in exile, says under this scenario, the country would be governed by a handful of powerful elite clans in alliance with business interests.

This last option, of course, is the one that many tycoons want. "They'd like to return to a time when they were listened to, when they were not stripped of assets and when they understood the rules of the game," says Prokopenko, who has spent a lot of time speaking to Russia's richest people.

Though their power has been seriously curtailed since the 1990s, it's still worth listening to the tycoons: given their immense wealth, it seems likely that sooner or later they will try to re-assert their political influence.

Already, some are "trying to be friends with the right sort of security officials or ministers", says Nekrasov, the exiled politician. But he says any further steps are "too dangerous to take".

He says the behaviour of the tycoons in coming years will depend in part on their finances. Those who have lots of liquid cash will be more confident to "play political games" and jockey for position, preparing for a post-Putin country. But those whose wealth is dependent on state contracts or government goodwill will feel too afraid, in case they lose everything, he says.

Prokopenko says there's already been a shift in how the businessmen talk about Putin. They used to nickname him "Nachalnik" (which translates as "boss"), as well as "Perviy" ("first"), or by his initials "VV" - all nicknames that convey a degree of respect. Now they call him "Ded", with what Prokopenko calls "a pinch of contempt". "Ded" translates as "oldie" or "granddad" - a much less reverent name.

Some rich Russians are pining after a "return of politics into people's lives", she says, with less repression, more open speech, and healthier competition between parties and politicians.

But at the moment, she says, they are too afraid to make that happen due to Russia's stifling atmosphere. Prokopenko interviewed one tycoon who physically sat on his phone during the whole conversation, because he thought it would make digital eavesdropping more difficult for secret police. "I thought that it's an absolutely Stalinistic type of fear. It's absolutely irrational," she says.

items.title: Skydio's asymmetrical F10 Lightrunner solves a problem with fixed-wing drones
items.summary: Article URL: https://spectrum.ieee.org/skydio-f10-lightrunner-asymmetrical-drone Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50512296 Points: 31 # Comments: 2
items.content:
The F10 Lightrunner’s weird asymmetry solves a key problem with fixed-wing drones

Skydio’s F10 autonomous camera drone can provide better quality video than any other fixed-wing drone, thanks to its lopsided design.

Skydio’s drones have always been magical. From MIT research and early prototypes to what I would argue is still the most advanced consumer drone ever made , this is a company that makes very cool stuff. Sadly, Skydio no longer makes cool stuff for consumers , instead focusing on drone platforms for public safety, inspection, and other things that, on a good day, don’t affect me personally.

Even so, a new drone from Skydio is worth paying attention to, especially when it’s as weird as this one—the F10 Lightrunner is a fixed-wing camera drone designed for autonomous deployment and high-speed flight, all while looking so lopsided that it’s surprising that it can actually fly.

There’s a short rabbit hole you can go down if you start looking for other examples of asymmetrical aircraft. In the 1990s, legendary aircraft designer Burt Rutan and his company Scaled Composites built some decidedly odd airplanes, including the Model 202 Boomerang . But perhaps the most famous asymmetrical aircraft was the Blohm & Voss BV 141 , a World War II-era reconnaissance plane that featured an engine in the middle alongside a crew compartment alarmingly offset out onto the right wing. The unique design was intended to give the crew the best possible view for reconnaissance missions, because in a typical single-engine aircraft, the crew sits right behind the engine, limiting forward visibility.

Nearly 90 years later, the Skydio F10 is applying a similar philosophy to fixed-wing reconnaissance drones, which typically track targets by flying around them in circles. “While turning at low altitudes, it becomes very hard to avoid occluding a camera with a wing or a tail,” explains Andrew Goessling , director of engineering at Skydio. “So we were analyzing a lot of these use cases, and one of our engineers just blurted out, ‘What if we put the camera on the wingtip?’ And that’s where it all started, because as long as you only turn left, a lot of these problems just go away.”

Of course, putting the camera on the F10’s wingtip creates a bunch of new problems, chief among them that the aircraft is no longer balanced. Not only is the camera payload fairly heavy relative to the total mass of the drone, but its bulk also creates greater drag. This is why the seemingly straightforward solution of putting something else (like a battery) on the other wingtip to rebalance the drone isn’t practical, says Goessling. “The issue there is that the camera represents a substantial portion of the total aircraft drag, so putting something else on the other wing would cut your flight time nearly in half.”

The F10’s wing-mounted camera payload necessitated asymmetrical wings and uneven motor placement. Skydio

Goessling points out that there’s nothing inherently bad about an asymmetric design like the F10; it just makes the life of engineers either a little more difficult or a little more exciting, depending on your perspective. “There were really two challenges here: What is the optimal design for an aircraft with a wingtip camera, and then once you have the design, how are you going to control it?”

Any fixed-wing aircraft design has to consider three factors: distribution of mass, how thrust is distributed between the motors, and how the shape and location of the wings affect the aircraft’s aerodynamics . Once Skydio decided on their requirements for the F10—including the wingtip camera, two motors to enable controllable hovering for takeoff and landing, and a high top speed and long flight time—the engineers used a modeling-and-optimization approach to explore design options. The resulting aircraft compensates for the wing-mounted camera payload by extending just that wing to provide more lift on that side, and repositioning the motors asymmetrically to balance thrust against the added drag of the camera.

The MegaDock can autonomously launch, recover, and recharge up to five F10 drones using a robot arm to grab them out of the air. Skydio

An added challenge was getting the F10 to launch and recover with a robot arm, using a storage, charging, and deployment system called the MegaDock. That requires the drone to transition from hover to forward flight and then back again—a particularly difficult trick for a flying wing with no tail control surfaces (movable parts of the wing used to steer the aircraft). The F10 uses model predictive control (a control technique based on a detailed physics model of the robot) to accomplish this autonomously, and a single control policy can handle the robot all the way through its entire flight envelope, from a stationary hover to its maximum flight speed of 100 miles per hour. In other words, there’s no “hover mode” or “flight mode,” so the mission planner just tells the drone where it needs to be, and the drone will know how to get itself there.

In operation, Skydio’s MegaDock can handle up to five F10s, allowing for continuous flight operations with three drones while two recharge. The entire system is fully autonomous, with humans only needed for remote supervisory control, communicating with the F10 via dual 5G cellular modems . Maximum flight time is 2 hours, and the aircraft is equipped with the same kind of magical obstacle-dodging camera setup as Skydio’s quadrotor drones. If something goes seriously wrong, an integrated parachute in the F10’s butt will deploy, lowering the drone to the ground gently enough to safely fly over people.

Goessling is the first to acknowledge that the F10 Lightrunner is an unconventional design, but he’s proud of what he and his team have come up with as a commercially viable solution to the occlusion issue with other fixed-wing drones. “It looks weird, and we got some pushback from some of the less technical parts of the company,” Goessling says. “If there were less crazy ways of doing it, we would have pursued them. But we have the data. We have sound reasons for every decision we’ve made. And the outcome at the end was well worth it.”

Evan Ackerman is a senior editor at IEEE Spectrum . Since 2007, he has written over 6,000 articles on robotics and technology. He has a degree in Martian geology and is excellent at playing bagpipes.
